# P1-054 — Certificate pinning

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted (Tope) |
| Date | 2026-10-22 |
| Cards | P1-054, P1-055 |
| RTM ids | EP-§13.1-22, EP-§13.1-23, EP-§13.1-24 |
| Sources | `ELEVATION.md#§13.1:L1863-L1866` |

## Decision
Both platforms pin the leaf certificate with SHA-256 of the DER, formatted `sha256/<base64>`. `CERTIFICATE_PIN_HASHES` holds the current pin and the next pin, comma-separated. A release that has at least one pin fails closed. A build with no pins stays open. The Dart client is the check on iOS and Android. The static Android pin-set is not filled in, because the hashes are a build secret and a placeholder is not a pin.

## Options considered
| Option | For | Against | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leaf DER, current plus next pin, open only when unset | Matches the app and `tool/print_ssl_pin.dart`. Rotation does not wait on a store release of a single pin. | The leaf must be updated at renewal. | Low |
| SPKI pinning | Survives leaf renewal. | Dart's `X509Certificate` does not expose the public key. A new parser would be a second mechanism. | High |
| Fail closed with no pin configured | Nothing ships unpinned. | Local and CI builds with an empty secret would not start. | High |

## Consequences
Android `network_security_config.xml` does not embed a pin. iOS `Info.plist` has no pin key; release ATS already disallows arbitrary loads. A mismatch throws `certificate_pin_mismatch`. Either configured pin is enough.

## Verification
`test/services/network/pinning_client_test.dart` rejects an unknown leaf and accepts the backup pin. An empty pin list allows the connection.
